summary: Modern databases increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer, allowing users to train models, generate embeddings, run inference, and invoke large language models using familiar SQL or native APIs without moving data to external platforms. A major trend is native vector search for semantic similarity and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), though some platforms only support vectors via extensions. These integrations reduce data movement, simplify ML pipelines, and bring generative AI directly to enterprise data.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides fully managed LLM and ML functions accessible via SQL and Python, including Cortex Analyst (natural language to SQL), Cortex Search (hybrid semantic retrieval), AI SQL functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), and Cortex Agents for building AI applications on governed data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake provides a built-in VECTOR data type plus vector distance functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE, VECTOR_INNER_PRODUCT), and Cortex Search offers a managed vector/hybrid search service.
databases.llm_integration: Native access to hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others) via Cortex functions; no external API keys required and data stays within Snowflake's governance boundary.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based: Cortex LLM functions billed per token (credits), and vector/search/embedding operations consume credits based on compute and serving. Billed in Snowflake credits on top of standard storage and compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization, boosted trees, deep neural nets) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted foundation models (Gemini) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model functions for inference directly in SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest neighbor search over embeddings stored in BigQuery tables.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models through remote models and functions like ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, enabling generative AI and embedding generation from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Charged by bytes processed or slot usage for model training/inference; Vertex AI remote model calls incur separate Vertex AI prediction charges. Vector search and index operations consume standard query/storage pricing.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL, while pgai (from Timescale) adds in-database functions to create embeddings and call LLMs (e.g., OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic) directly from SQL, along with pgai Vectorizer for automated embedding pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-to-extension. Core PostgreSQL has no built-in vector search, but pgvector is an open-source extension providing a vector data type with exact and ANN indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat). Since it is the de facto standard extension installable on most PostgreSQL deployments, it is widely considered first-class, though technically delivered via extension.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai, PostgreSQL can call external LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, Hugging Face) from SQL for embedding generation, completion, and RAG workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Both extensions are open source and free; costs are the underlying PostgreSQL compute/storage plus any external LLM provider API fees incurred by pgai calls.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML enables SQL functions that invoke Amazon SageMaker models and Amazon Comprehend (sentiment analysis) directly from queries in Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing inference to be applied to row data without exporting it.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Aurora ML. Vector similarity search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only through the pgvector extension, which is a separate open-source extension rather than a native Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in LLM functions in Aurora ML itself; LLM/foundation-model access is achieved indirectly by invoking SageMaker-hosted models or by using Amazon Bedrock integration via pgvector/aws_ml extension functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Aurora charge for the ML integration; you pay standard Aurora compute/storage plus the underlying SageMaker or Comprehend inference costs for invoked models.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML lets users create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, leveraging Amazon SageMaker (including Autopilot) behind the scenes. It supports regression, classification, and bringing custom/remote SageMaker models, plus integration with Bedrock for generative AI via SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search / ANN index type in Redshift. Similarity can be approximated manually, but there is no built-in vector data type or dedicated vector search function comparable to native vector databases.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock to invoke foundation models (e.g., for text generation and embeddings) from SQL, and can call remote LLM-backed SageMaker endpoints for inference.
databases.pricing_notes: Model training incurs SageMaker costs; in-database (local) inference runs within Redshift compute at no extra inference charge, while remote model and Bedrock calls incur their respective service charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Model Serving, Foundation Model APIs, Agent Framework, and AI functions (ai_query, ai_gen) callable from SQL. Databricks Vector Search is a managed service for indexing and querying embeddings integrated with Unity Catalog.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, built-in vector database that automatically syncs with Delta tables and supports ANN similarity search governed by Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to hosted and third-party LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Anthropic, OpenAI via external models), with SQL AI functions and the Mosaic AI Agent Framework for RAG and agents.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search, Model Serving, and Foundation Model APIs are billed separately (pay-per-token or provisioned throughput) on top of underlying compute.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables semantic similarity search by storing embeddings alongside operational data in MongoDB documents and querying them with the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, supporting ANN search, pre-filtering, and hybrid search for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is a built-in feature of MongoDB Atlas, using a dedicated vector index type and the $vectorSearch operator integrated into the aggregation pipeline (powered by Atlas Search/Lucene HNSW).
databases.llm_integration: No bundled LLM, but tight integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and major model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) for generating embeddings and building RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas dedicated clusters; vector search runs on Search Nodes (or cluster resources) billed as part of Atlas cluster/Search infrastructure, with no per-query LLM charge from MongoDB (external embedding/model costs apply).
